title: Burst fairness: per-tenant SLA throttles, provisional boost accounting, and invoice breakdown UI
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Customers on Dedicated fleets have had unpredictable invoices when tenant traffic spikes trigger provisional burst capacity. We need a coordinated system that enforces per-tenant throughput fairness during burst windows, accounts for provisional boosts in a transparent way, and surfaces a clear invoice-level breakdown in the Console so operators and customers can reconcile charges quickly. This ticket defines throttles and multipliers at the request-routing layer, the accounting tags emitted to metering, and the Console UI to expose those tags on invoices and per-route cost views.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant burst throttle implemented: soft SLA threshold + hard cap that can be configured per-reservation
Provisional boost events are tagged with boost_id and boost_type in metering pipeline
Billing system produces line items that attribute tokens to: baseline capacity, provisional boost, and overage (if any)
Console invoice view includes expandable boost line items with explanation text and link to burst events
Operator view shows active boost pools, remaining boost budget, and top consumers with per-tenant fairness score
E2E tests simulate a 30-minute spike and produce reproducible, human-readable invoice artifacts
implementation_notes: Design choices and trade-offs: 1) Enforce a configurable soft SLA at 95th percentile of normal throughput; once exceeded, requests are tagged as 'boosted' and routed to surge lane. 2) Hard cap prevents individual tenants from consuming >X% of a fleet's provisional pool; value defaults to 40% but is overrideable by contract. 3) Metering tags: boost_id, boost_bucket (surge_pool_name), boost_weight (multiplier), origin_sla_reason. 4) Billing will prorate provisional boost cost by weighted usage; invoices must show both raw token counts and cost after discounting reserved commit. 5) To avoid double-billing during quick retries, dedupe boost events by request_id and session TTL. 6) Autoscaler integration: provisional pool consumption contributes to short-term scale signals but does not immediately trigger new reserved allocations without operator approval.
implementation_steps: Add per-tenant soft SLA checks to request router and emit boost tag on decision path
Implement server-side hard cap enforcement in lane broker with config flags and feature gate
Extend meter pipeline to accept boost tags and emit consolidated boost_id line items to billing warehouse
Billing: add boost attribution step to billing job and generate invoice delta table for March release
Console: build invoice breakdown component and operator dashboard card for active boost pools
Add canary rollout for a single dedicated cluster and monitor for billing regressions
test_plan: Unit tests for router decision logic and hard cap enforcement
Integration test that starts a provisional boost event, routes traffic to surge lane, and verifies metering tags
E2E scenario: 10 tenants with synthetic traffic patterns, escalate one tenant to 60% of pool and assert hard cap throttles it back
Billing validation job comparing pre- and post-change invoice line items for a known spike trace
Manual QA: Ops runs the console explainer and confirms links to burst event logs
monitoring_and_alerting: New SLO: burst fairness score (median tenant share during active boost) must be >= 0.6
Alert: boost pool consumed > 90% for more than 5 minutes
Alert: unexpected invoice delta > 15% vs forecast during canary
Dashboard: per-pool consumption, top 10 tenant shares, recent boost events stream
rollout_notes: Canary timeline: 48h in staging, 72h in a single low-risk dedicated cluster (non-enterprise), then gradated rollouts across regions. Billing feature is off by default for existing customers; opt-in via contract or Console toggle. Communication plan: ops runbook + email to active Dedicated customers explaining invoice format change and how to interpret boost line items.
